content.text: {"label":"unknown_supply_issue","explanation":"Demand is normal: volume is at or below forecast on both queues (payments -7.6% today, general -1.7%), AHT is close to forecast, and the only incident is a resolved overnight batch. Service level fell (payments 69% at 10:45, general 62-72% since 10:15) because staffing is about 25% short on both queues. Attendance shows 14 payments and 9 general absences against about 2.5 usual, mostly late arrivals noted as a bus strike. Sick calls (3 per queue) are near normal, so this is not a sick wave. It is a supply shortfall from late or absent agents that may last into the afternoon. The 08:30 levers (break delays, coaching cancellations, payments overtime) have mostly expired, which partly explains the 10:45 drop on payments.","plan_name":"Supply-shortfall cover on both queues, 11:00-15:30","rationale":"Both queues are about 10 agents short, so there is no spare capacity to move cross-skilled agents between them. The plan adds paid capacity and frees agent time. Consecutive overtime offers on both queues: about 4 then 3 accepted agents per queue for 2 h each, roughly Rs 10,400. With about Rs 2,900 already spent, the day stays under the Rs 15,000 budget. Coaching is cancelled for the middle of the day, and breaks that have not yet been delayed are pushed 30 min to smooth the noon peak. IVR callback and chat deflection of simple status and enquiry reasons trim the incoming workload at low cost. Overtime approved now arrives at 11:30, so the other levers start at 11:00 to cover the gap. Late agents should arrive progressively, so the levers end by mid-afternoon rather than running all day. The 11:25 fraud-awareness social post may add a few fraud_report calls on payments, which this cover should
